answer: A comet beacon salts each identity's challenge by address, so one precomputed proof cannot serve a thousand clones. A relic is the non-transferable chain of past honest attestations; a fresh clone holds no relic and must earn one round by round, so history cannot be bought. Each answer is signed by a quill key bound to the relic; if one quill signs two conflicting answers, the whole cluster is slashed together, penalty growing with the square of cluster size. N clones therefore cost N relic chains, N bonds, and N squared in correlated slash risk — superlinear by construction, not by delay.
